title: See How Compound Growth Works
blurb: Understand how returns can build on earlier returns—and why they are not guaranteed.
cards: i
Growth can build on growth
With compounding, returns that remain invested may themselves earn returns later. The effect depends on time, rate, fees, taxes and whether returns are positive.
i
Start early, stay realistic
Time can make regular contributions more powerful, but investments can fall in value. A calculator illustration is not a promise or a forecast.
e
A simple illustration
If 100 grew by 5% for one year, it would become 105 before fees and taxes. If it then grew by 5% again, 5% would apply to 105, producing 110.25. Real investment returns do not arrive as a steady 5%.
q
What does compounding mean in this example?
Only the original amount can grow
Earlier returns may also earn returns
Investments cannot lose value
Growth is guaranteed each month
Compounding is growth on the original amount and on returns left invested.
t
A compound growth calculator guarantees the result it displays.
It illustrates assumptions. Actual returns, fees and taxes may differ, and investment values can fall.
q
What happens if fees increase, while all else is equal?
More of the return stays invested
Less of the return remains for growth
Risk disappears
The result is guaranteed
Fees reduce the amount left invested to grow over time.
